title: Cinema equalizers and using ribbon mic proximity for bass
summary: He found motion-picture equalizers and a filter, and before that used ribbon-mic proximity effect to get low end on vocalists.

story.theme_name: In the studio: making records, then and now
story.community_name: Making records: studios, takes and the technology

blocks.x: None of that. Absolutely nothing. And then, like I say, through this digging into the motion picture thing, I got a hold of... There was a company called Cinema that used Western Electric and IRPE patents and built equalizers for the motion picture industry.

And the motion picture industry used equalizers like this, presence, which would be 3 and 5K, boost or dip. If somebody had a tinny sounding voice, you could actually dip that a little bit and make them maybe sound more rounded. Low end for generally music, not voices. Very few people, you want to boost the low end. And there was a way to do that, incidentally, without EQ, and I did that before I had EQ, is that the ribbon microphones are a velocity microphone.
They detect the velocity of the air particles. That's because they... That's why you have the ribbon. That's right. Yeah, the ribbon does that. Yeah. It's very light ribbon being flooded by the...
But it's very sensitive as well.

Yeah, right. Well, since they have a velocity microphone, if you got up close to it, it would accentuate the low end. So... And the old-time radio operators used to do it. They'd get right up close to a microphone and don't talk right into it because it would
pop, you know? Mm-hmm. And they'd get that big...

Deep voice, right. ...old-time radio announcer sound. Right. Yeah. And I found out about that. So I used it by getting vocalists to be up close if they needed some low-end bump or that kind of thing. Mm-hmm. And then, like I said, I got ahold of a couple of cinema equalizers and a filter. Mm-hmm. And that helped things. But then I could only use it after the mix. Or what I finally did was buy a separate microphone preamp for the vocalist so I could use it because I'd have to bring it up to line level to use these. These were line level things. Mm-hmm. They couldn't use them on microphones the way consoles do, you know, single microphone input. You could take that one microphone and do things. Well, so I had this one microphone preamp for the vocalist. And I could run... Then I got up line level. So I could do things with the equalizers and filters on the vocal. Again, minimally. These filters are very good for the quality of them. Filters and equalizers also introduce phase shift. Mm-hmm. So you have to be careful there, too.
